title: A mighty king and the fourfold division of his kingdom (Dan 11:3–4)
speaker: The man clothed in linen
description: A mighty king rules with great dominion; at his height his kingdom is broken toward the four winds, not to his posterity.
in_text_interpretation: The text does not name the king; it parallels the goat's great horn (8:8, 21–22), which the text calls "the first king" of Greece.

interpretations.label: Alexander the Great and the partition among his generals
interpretations.framework: Common to patristic, historicist, critical and evangelical interpreters
interpretations.summary: Alexander died young and his heirs did not inherit; the empire was divided among his generals (Jerome: Ptolemy, Philip Arrhidaeus, Seleucus, Antigonus; Newton: Ptolemy, Antigonus, Lysimachus, Cassander, with Seleucus later). "Others besides these" (11:4) = lesser kingdoms (Jerome). Acceptance: no dissent found among sources consulted.
